questions.q: Which CloudWatch metric shows how far behind real-time a Kinesis consumer has fallen?
questions.explain: IteratorAge measures the age of the last record a consumer processed relative to now — a climbing IteratorAge means the consumer is falling behind the stream.

questions.q: Which metric would you watch to catch DMS change data capture falling behind the source database?
questions.explain: Replication lag directly measures how far behind the source database DMS's CDC replication has fallen.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what actually separates a 'working demo' from a production pipeline?
options: The pipeline surviving real-world failure conditions and telling someone when it doesn't, not just working once on clean data
Using a larger number of AWS services in the architecture
Running the pipeline in a different AWS region
Having a higher AWS budget allocated to it
questions.explain: A demo only has to succeed once under known-good conditions; a production pipeline has to keep working under real-world failure conditions and surface a signal when it doesn't — which is what monitoring provides.

questions.q: In the end-to-end monitoring story this lesson builds, what completes the loop after a metric crosses a meaningful threshold?
options: An alarm transitioning state and an SNS notification reaching an actual person
The metric being deleted from CloudWatch automatically
The pipeline shutting itself down permanently
Nothing further is needed once a metric exists
questions.explain: A metric alone doesn't close the loop — it takes an alarm watching it and an SNS notification (or similar action) reaching someone who can respond.

questions.q: What is the next and final course in this path after AWS Data Engineering, according to this lesson's outro?
questions.explain: This lesson closes AWS Data Engineering and points to the AWS Capstone course, where the services covered across this course are combined into one built pipeline.
